turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Ranchers watch the Baja 1000 trucks tear up the dirt roads they use every day.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The governor says the state will not pay for repairs again.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: He wants the organiser to cover it through agreements with the towns.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Ranchers get the damage but no direct benefit from the race.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: In town, paving crews pick the streets with the most cars first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Hospitals and schools come next when the budget runs out.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Sepuimm says the street that links a neighbourhood to the main road usually gets done first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Asphalt work on Boulevard Pino Pallas should finish before Christmas.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Calle Francisco King in hydraulic concrete will take about four months.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today on transport, what is a road for?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Luz, the paving decisions in La Paz caught my eye.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Palabra BCS reports that Sepuimm head Carolina Armenta Cervantes ties priorities to traffic volume, flood zones, hospitals and schools.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Demand exceeds resources, so they start with streets that link to main arteries.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Asphalt work on Boulevard Pino Pallas should finish before Christmas. Calle Francisco King, in hydraulic concrete, will take about four months.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. How does that affect daily life for people in those neighbourhoods?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It eases the worst commutes first, yet leaves many side streets waiting.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Now the governor and the Baja 1000.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HOY BCS says Víctor Castro wants the organisers to repair rural roads damaged by the race and states the state will not subsidise that damage again.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Ranchers carry the cost without direct gain.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: He acknowledged the race brings spending and visibility, yet asked for agreements with municipalities to cover repairs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does that shift mean for the long road south?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México adds that air fares in La Paz rose 26.36 percent last month, pushing local inflation to 1.17 percent.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert light falls hard on those unpaved stretches.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Electricity prices jumped 18.51 percent after summer subsidies ended, and annual inflation in La Paz sits at 3.16 percent, below the national 3.75 percent.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. What about the new energy project in Mulegé?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: PVTIME reports CFE and HDF Energy launched a tender for the Oasis microgrid: 72 MW solar, 80 MWh batteries and a 20 MW electrolyser turning surplus into green hydrogen.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That could change how power moves along the peninsula.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It aims to serve about 40,000 households and cut 94,000 tonnes of CO2 each year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Does the road feel different when the light changes like that?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The stories keep pointing to one line.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Which line?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The road that runs the length of the peninsula, and the water that touches it.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias reported rain and sewage damaging the Transpeninsular shoulders near San José. Diario Humano covered residents fighting to keep the East Cape coastal route in the 2040 plan.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Residents plan to collect signatures 19 to 22 November under the slogan The Coastal Road stays.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes. They want the route kept as a rustic scenic drive with beach access. Grupo Questro proposed an alternative at least one kilometre inland.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And yet the same highway is the only spine mentioned in the dossiers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: El Economista noted that 90% of goods reach Baja California Sur by sea. Baja Ferries carries over 200,000 passengers a year and wants to turn the crossings into a longer stay.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The ferry aims for 300–400,000 passengers with cruise-style packages and an alliance with the Chepe train.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the thread is not only asphalt.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The knowledge graph shows the Transpeninsular conditioned by protected areas and budget. The coastal road debate is the same question in a different place.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But here is the thing. Even when we talk about buses in La Paz or repairs after the Baja 1000, the quiet partner remains the ferry schedule and the port.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The design underneath is land and water held together by one slow corridor.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Did you know the state just announced new buses for La Paz public transport, set to arrive around March 2026?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is a quiet shift. Think of the daily ride to work or the market. One smoother bus instead of three old ones idling at the same stop. The announcement came during Sheinbaum’s tour and report to the people of Baja California Sur.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. What does that change for the road itself?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It lines up with the announced repaving of the Transpeninsular highway, also under the same program. A road that carries people and water trucks alike. Does the desert notice the difference when the surface stays even after the next storm?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A road that carries people and water trucks alike. Does the desert notice the difference?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Fewer stops, less dust on the shoulder. The same long stretch south, only now the surface stays even after the next storm. The repaving program was detailed right alongside the bus news in that same state report.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the timing? What else lines up on that same stretch?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Both the buses and the resurfacing were detailed in the recent state report from Sheinbaum’s tour. One even surface, fewer idling engines, and the desert light stays clear a little longer each morning.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s Visión reads mobility as the thread that could keep Baja California Sur whole toward 2050, but only if it stops repeating the same coastal line from south to north.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the numbers already point to where that line is thinning.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: SJD traffic dropped 4.6 percent in October and 5.5 percent from January through October, while LAP traffic rose 8.7 percent year to date. The portal notes the news flow on mobility is mixed.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the weight is already moving.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The aspiration is simple. Use La Paz as a measured counterweight to the SJD axis. Let Sea of Cortez ferries and cabotage carry freight and passengers where the projects are already underway. Let paving serve the towns that are already there.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would have to hold for that polycentric shape to last?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Each place keeps its own role. New growth only where water and energy show clear margin. East Cape and Loreto stay inside ANP and POEL limits. Comondú and the north add production and energy without pulling services away.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the plans that could still shift the balance?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: El Tezal partial plan now in public consultation and the Los Cabos urban plan update with its density limits and the Cabo del Este coastal road.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The roads we choose decide which towns grow.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Sepuimm says street paving is decided mainly by traffic volume. Governor Víctor Castro demands the Baja 1000 repair rural roads and says the state will not subsidise the race again.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Residents in the East Cape are fighting to keep their coastal route in the 2040 urban plan.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Rain and sewage spills damage the Transpeninsular highway in Los Cabos. La Paz council approves two buses to extend the Tiburón Urbano service to El Centenario and Chametla. Baja Ferries wants to turn Sea of Cortez crossings into a holiday experience.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the takeaway is simple: connectivity serves the whole state, not only the SJD–Los Cabos axis.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. Stay with us. More Radio BCS2050 after the music.
